section: Tribunals - Articles 323A and 323B; administrative and specialised tribunals; tribunal reforms
subsections: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals
Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches

accepted.s: The Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) derives its legal basis from which of the following provisions?
o: Article 262 and the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
Article 315 and the Central Civil Services Act, 1985
Article 323A and the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
Article 323B and the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021
accepted.x: CAT is empowered by Article 323A and was established under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985. It is a statutory and quasi-judicial body.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional enabling provision with the parent statute instead of confusing Articles 323A and 323B.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Central Administrative Tribunal was set up in 1985 during the Prime Ministership of:
accepted.x: The CAT was set up in 1985 under Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. It was not established during Lal Bahadur Shastri's tenure.
accepted.tq: Use the year–office-holder association and guard against a swapped Prime Minister trap.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition of the Central Administrative Tribunal:
1. It has 69 Members.
2. There are 35 Judicial Members, including the Chairperson.
3. There are 34 Administrative Members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The CAT has 69 Members comprising 35 Judicial Members, including the Chairperson, and 34 Administrative Members.
accepted.tq: Check the total and its two component figures before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the eligibility of members of the Central Administrative Tribunal?
o: Judicial Members must be district judges, while Administrative Members must have served at the level of Joint Secretary only.
Judicial Members must be serving Supreme Court judges, while Administrative Members must be serving Cabinet Secretaries.
Judicial Members must be qualified as High Court judges, while Administrative Members must have served at the level of Additional Secretary or above.
Both categories of Members must be serving members of the Union Public Service Commission.
accepted.x: Judicial Members must possess qualifications equivalent to those of High Court judges. Administrative Members require service at the level of Additional Secretary or above.
accepted.tq: Separate the judicial and administrative eligibility streams rather than applying one qualification to both.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Central Administrative Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. Its main Bench is located at New Delhi.
2. It has 18 outlying Benches.
3. It has jurisdiction over service disputes of civilian defence employees, but not armed forces personnel.
4. It exercises jurisdiction over notified public sector undertakings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. CAT has its main Bench at New Delhi and 18 outlying Benches, and its jurisdiction includes specified Central and All-India service matters, civilian defence employees and notified PSUs, but excludes armed forces personnel.
accepted.tq: Test jurisdiction by separating included civilian categories from the expressly excluded armed forces personnel.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The jurisdiction of the Central Administrative Tribunal primarily extends to recruitment and service matters relating to which of the following?
1. All-India Services
2. Central civil services and civil posts under the Union
3. Civilian defence employees
4. Notified public sector undertakings
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: CAT deals with recruitment and service matters concerning all four categories listed. Armed forces personnel, however, are outside this stated jurisdiction.
accepted.tq: Build the answer by identifying every category specifically included in the tribunal's service jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the procedure followed by the Central Administrative Tribunal is correct?
o: It is strictly bound by the Code of Civil Procedure and prohibits personal appearance of litigants.
It is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, follows the principles of natural justice, charges nominal fees and permits parties to appear in person.
It is not bound by any legal principles and imposes court-level fees in every case.
It follows only criminal procedure and permits appearance only through senior advocates.
accepted.x: CAT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure. It follows natural justice, charges nominal filing fees and permits litigants to appear in person.
accepted.tq: Identify the tribunal's simplified procedure by rejecting absolute claims about CPC, fees and representation.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The disposal rate of the Central Administrative Tribunal mentioned in the context of its performance is:
accepted.x: The stated disposal rate of CAT is 92.9 per cent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precise percentage from nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: After the decision in L. Chandra Kumar (1997), appeals against decisions of the Central Administrative Tribunal lie first to the:
o: High Court through a Division Bench
President of India through a constitutional reference
Central Government through a departmental appeal
accepted.x: Following L. Chandra Kumar (1997), CAT decisions are subject to review by the High Court through a Division Bench, with a further appeal to the Supreme Court where applicable. They do not go directly to the Supreme Court.
accepted.tq: Track the appellate sequence and reject the direct-to-Supreme-Court trap.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 10th All India Conference of the Central Administrative Tribunal was held at:
accepted.x: The 10th All India Conference of CAT was held in New Delhi.
accepted.tq: Test the specific venue of the conference rather than the location of an outlying Bench.
accepted.sec: Central Administrative Tribunal - legal basis, members, jurisdiction, when set up, appeals  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Armed Forces Tribunal — Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007
Debt Recovery Tribunal — Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
accepted.x: The Armed Forces Tribunal was established under the Armed Forces Tribunal Act, 2007. The Companies Act, 2013 relates to NCLT/NCLAT, the Customs Act, 1962 to CESTAT, and the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 to CGIT-cum-Labour Courts.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure parent-Act pair and eliminate tribunals associated with other enactments.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Armed Forces Tribunal, consider the following statements:
1. Its Principal Bench is located at New Delhi.
2. It has Regional Benches at Jaipur, Jabalpur and Guwahati.
3. It has a Regional Bench at Bhopal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Armed Forces Tribunal has no Bench at Bhopal.
accepted.tq: Use the NOT-present location as the trap after confirming the Principal Bench and recognised Regional Benches.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the Regional Benches of the Armed Forces Tribunal?
accepted.x: Bhopal does not have an Armed Forces Tribunal Bench. The listed Regional Benches include Chandigarh, Lucknow and Srinagar, among others.
accepted.tq: Find the absent location by comparing each option with the stated Regional Bench list.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. NCLT and NCLAT — Companies Act, 2013
2. CESTAT — Customs Act, 1962
3. CGIT-cum-Labour Courts — Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
4. Debt Recovery Tribunals — Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These enactments provide the statutory basis identified for the respective tribunal arrangements.
accepted.tq: Verify each tribunal against its parent enactment, using the statutory title as the decisive clue.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Company Law Tribunal and the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal were set up in:
accepted.x: NCLT and NCLAT were set up in 2016 under the framework of the Companies Act, 2013.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of the parent Act from the later year in which the tribunals were set up.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following functions is associated with the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT)?
o: It hears only customs and excise appeals.
It hears appeals from NCLT and also appeals under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code and from the Competition Commission of India.
It hears only income-tax appeals under Article 323A.
It hears appeals exclusively from Debt Recovery Tribunals.
accepted.x: NCLAT hears appeals from NCLT and also deals with appeals under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code and appeals from the Competition Commission of India.
accepted.tq: Identify the appellate body's wider subject jurisdiction instead of limiting it to company-law appeals alone.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) deals with appeals relating to:
o: Income tax, company law and insolvency בלבד
Industrial disputes and provident fund alone
accepted.x: CESTAT hears appeals concerning customs, excise and service tax.
accepted.tq: Match the tribunal's abbreviated name and statutory field with its specific appellate subject.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Appeals from the Debt Recovery Tribunals lie to the:
o: Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal
accepted.x: Appeals from Debt Recovery Tribunals lie to the Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal (DRAT).
accepted.tq: Use the corresponding appellate-body name and avoid swapping DRAT with other specialised appellate tribunals.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) is correct?
o: It hears income-tax appeals, is an example associated with Article 323B and functions under the Law Ministry.
It hears customs appeals and functions under the Ministry of Defence.
It hears service disputes of All-India Services under Article 323A.
It hears company-law appeals and functions under the Ministry of Finance only.
accepted.x: ITAT deals with income-tax appeals, is cited as an example of a tribunal under Article 323B, and functions under the Law Ministry as stated.
accepted.tq: Combine the tribunal's subject, constitutional association and administrative ministry without swapping ministries.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central Government Industrial Tribunal-cum-Labour Courts:
1. There are 22 such courts.
2. They are constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
3. The Mumbai and Kolkata tribunals also function as National Tribunals.
4. They hear Employees' Provident Fund appeals since the Finance Act, 2017.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. There are 22 CGIT-cum-Labour Courts under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947; Mumbai and Kolkata also act as National Tribunals, and EPF appeals have been heard by them since the Finance Act, 2017.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical count, parent statute, special status of two tribunals and the stated starting year together.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following specialised tribunals in chronological order according to the parent enactments mentioned for them:
A. CESTAT — Customs Act, 1962
B. CGIT-cum-Labour Courts — Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
C. Debt Recovery Tribunals — 1993 enactment
D. NCLT/NCLAT — Companies Act, 2013
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Industrial Disputes Act, 1947; Customs Act, 1962; the 1993 debt-recovery enactment; and Companies Act, 2013. Therefore, the order is B, A, C, D.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest enactments first, then place the 1962 and 1993 laws between them.
accepted.sec: Specialised tribunals - parent Act and benches  [APPSC]
